title: Dabur — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
According to PissedConsumer, Dabur has a 1.8 star rating from 19 customer reviews, with common complaints including refund requests, delivery failures, damaged or poor quality products, and allegations of fraud and unresponsive customer service. Dabur's Digital Annual Report for 2023-24 mentions that 3,475 complaints were registered in fiscal 2022-23, with 3,460 resolved in the reporting year and the rest resolved amicably in the following month. DaburShop's contact page provides customer support email and phone number for issues, complaints, or refunds.

Dabur's three foreign subsidiaries are facing lawsuits in the U.S. and Canada over allegations that their hair-relaxer products caused ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, and other health issues. The lawsuits are in the pleadings and early discovery phases, with various motions pending. The company has stated that at this stage, any financial implications due to compensation or penalties cannot be determined. In a separate case, the Delhi High Court granted interim relief to Dabur by staying an FSSAI order that directed the company to stop using "100%" claims on several products, scheduling the next hearing for August 24.

According to Dabur, its subsidiaries – Namaste, Dermoviva and DINTL “deny liability” and have retained counsel to defend them in these lawsuits as “these allegations are based on unsubstantiated and incomplete study,” it added.

All these cases are in the pleadings and early discovery phases of litigation, which means the parties are challenging the adequacy of the plaintiffs' complaints and, in some cases, exchanging requests for information and documents. [...] SEE ALL  Remove

Shortly after the NIH study's initial results were published, a class action was filed against Dabur International in the Illinois federal court. The plaintiffs claim that their long-term use of chemical hair relaxer products manufactured and marketed by Dabur International caused the development of uterine cancer or ovarian cancer. Plaintiffs claim that the company failed to warn consumers that its hair straightening products, such as the ORS Olive Oil hair relaxers, contain [...] The lawsuits against Dabur International were filed after the Sister Study was published in the Journal of the National Cancer Institute. The study published on October 17, 2022, found that ingredients in hair relaxer products contain endocrine-disrupting and carcinogenic chemicals that can lead to the development of hormone-sensitive diseases such as:

 uterine cancer (endometrial cancer, uterine sarcoma)
 ovarian cancer (non-serous and serous tumors) [...] Those who intend to file a toxic hair relaxer claim against Dabur International must meet the following eligibility requirements:

 they must have used Dabur International chemical hair relaxers for at least 2 - 5 years
 they must have used Dabur International hair relaxers at least four times a year
 they must have been diagnosed with uterine cancer or ovarian cancer
